page: Microsoft Azure E32ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the Env6 series, designed for network optimization and enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory density. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The compute configuration delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled (2 threads per core). Cache resources include a massive 260 MB L3 cache, complemented by 2 MB L2 cache and 48 KB L1 data cache per core. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512, AMX-TILE, and AMX-INT8.

The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of memory, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture relies entirely on remote disk attachments, as the instance includes no local storage. Graphic accelerators are omitted, with a GPU count of zero. Benchmark evaluations show strong memory bandwidth on uncached large-block reads (192.86 GB/sec) and elevated performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (205.46 GB/sec), PassMark physics testing (6,703.98), and static web serving throughput (56.03 GB/sec). Large-block write bandwidth reaches 84.16 GB/sec, while in-memory throughput achieves 40.94 million Redis SET operations per second.

In artificial intelligence workloads, the instance leverages its Intel AMX capabilities to perform well on lightweight parameter models, achieving top-tier text generation on small 135M models (381.68 tokens/sec) and strong prompt processing on medium 7B models (200.75 tokens/sec). Conversely, text generation with large 70B models falls to a poor tier at 2.56 tokens/sec due to memory bus bottlenecks and the absence of discrete GPU acceleration. The lack of integrated ephemeral storage represents an operational tradeoff requiring explicit network-attached storage provisioning. Overall, the resource density makes the instance cost-efficient for large in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-throughput web proxies, and medium-scale enterprise analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ns_v6 is a memory-optimized, network-optimized virtual machine offering 32 vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz across 16 physical cores, the instance provides 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced vector and matrix instructions like AVX-512 and AMX, but includes no local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate strong uncached memory read bandwidth (192.86 GB/sec), high multi-threaded decompression throughput (205.46 GB/sec), and robust static web delivery (56.03 GB/sec), alongside 40.94 million Redis SET operations per second. While smaller language models leverage AMX instructions effectively, larger models experience diminished generation rates due to hardware limitations. Azure E32ns_v6 is primarily suited for in-memory databases, large caching layers, high-throughput network applications, and memory-intensive enterprise data processing.
